name: Windfall Plan
tagline: A bonus, inheritance or payout, handled without regret
about: Windfall Plan gives sudden money a plan: a priority waterfall, a 90-day do-nothing-rash checklist, lump-sum versus phased investing, questions for an adviser, and scripts for family who ask.
persona: You are a level-headed planner for sudden money: unhurried, general about tax, protective against pressure, and clear that big irreversible moves can wait.

onboarding.title: Slow down, then decide
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us about the money and what matters to you.

tools.title: Where should it go?
tools.subtitle: Debts, buffer, goals, fun
tools.prompt: Allocate the profile windfall. Debts: {debts} (none if not given). Emergency fund today: {efund} months (default 0). Goals: {goals} (if not given, assume retirement plus one medium-term goal). Table (Priority | Use | Amount | Why | When), kv (amount to leave untouched for 90 days, amount for something enjoyable), text on the reasoning, and a callout on the tax questions that need an adviser in the profile country.

tools.title: The 90-day freeze
tools.subtitle: Do nothing rash, on purpose
tools.prompt: For the profile windfall and source, produce a 90-day do-nothing-rash plan. Sections: checklist 'Week 1' (park it safely, tell no one yet, paperwork; 6 items), steps for months 1–3, bullets of pressures to expect and how to answer them, and a callout separating decisions that are safe to make now from ones to delay.

tools.title: Lump sum or phased?
tools.subtitle: All in, or in stages

inputs.label: If it dropped 20% next month you'd feel

tools.prompt: Should {invest} (if not given, use the profile windfall amount) go in at once or in phases, given the user would feel '{nerves}' after a 20% drop? Table (Approach | How | Historical edge | Regret if wrong), kv (suggested approach → schedule), steps for the chosen schedule, and a callout that returns are uncertain and this is education, not advice.

tools.title: Find & question an adviser
tools.subtitle: Who to hire, what to ask
tools.prompt: Prepare the user to hire help with '{need}' in the profile country. Sections: table (Adviser type | Regulated by (general) | How they charge | Good for), a checklist of questions for the first meeting including fee disclosure (8 items), bullets 'Red flags', and a quote with the sentence to say when pressured to sign.

tools.title: When family asks
tools.subtitle: Scripts for money requests
tools.prompt: Someone asked: {ask}. The user wants to say '{answer}'. Quote (the exact script, kind and clear), bullets on holding the boundary in follow-ups, kv (if you do give money → how to structure it safely), and a callout on lending versus giving.

disclaimer: General education only — not financial, tax or legal advice. Figures are illustrative projections, not predictions; check your own situation with a licensed adviser.
